artboards.title: Option E · Sidebar and floating chat
Option F · Tabs and chat rail

annotations.text: Round 2. Every option is a fixed 1440 by 900 application shell: no page scroll, the grid stretches to the viewport, and only long lists scroll inside their own card. Navigation for multiple areas is built in. Chat is a drawer, a floating panel, or a rail. Content is the same across options; doTERRA is sample data.

Option D · Rail and drawer
A 76 px icon rail for areas (Home, Weekly status, Milestones, RAID, Decisions, Artifacts, Catalog) with an engagement switcher in the top bar. Ask this project opens as a 360 px right drawer from the top bar and minimizes to a pill; the grid re-flows to three columns when it is closed (next artboard).
Trade-off: rail labels are terse, and the drawer takes a quarter of the width while open.

Option E · Sidebar and floating chat
A 248 px sidebar carries the engagement name, area navigation, and the seven lifecycle stages as a live list, which frees the main area from the journey strip. Chat floats bottom-right over content and minimizes to a pill.
Trade-off: the floating panel covers part of the evidence column while open, and the sidebar spends width on stage names that rarely change.

Option F · Tabs and chat rail
Area tabs under the top bar keep the full width for content; a persistent 340 px chat rail sits on the right and collapses to an edge tab. The journey strip stays in the main area.
Trade-off: least room for the Now panel, and a permanently visible chat gives a Beta capability the most real estate of the three.
Round 1, kept for reference. Rejected on Sep 6: these are scrolling pages and do not use the full viewport.
